This application is a server-rendered catalog management site with optional SQL Server persistence and Azure Blob image storage. The diagrams summarize the application layers and the principal interactions between its components.

Data Storage & External Services

SQL Server is the persistent store when mock data is disabled; the default configuration uses a mock catalog service. Azure Blob Storage is an optional image backend. Optional integrations include Microsoft Entra ID for sign-in, Azure Key Vault for configuration, and Application Insights for telemetry. No message broker or application cache is used by the catalog service.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac selects mock or database-backed catalog services and local or Azure image storage from configuration flags.
  • Entity Framework 6 and a SQL connection factory isolate persistence from the catalog pages.
  • The application is a single Web Forms deployment; service calls are in-process, with SQL Server and optional Azure services outside the process.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are the service-level domain entities used by the catalog pages and persistence layer. PaginatedItemsViewModel is the catalog listing response model. The image uploader accepts a multipart file and item identifier and returns a small JSON object containing the staged image name and URL. No immutable DTO records, OpenAPI/Swagger specifications, protobuf schemas, or GraphQL schemas were found. JavaScriptSerializer serializes the uploader response.

Communication Patterns

  • Synchronous: browser-to-Web-Forms HTTP requests, in-process calls from pages to catalog/image services, EF6 calls to SQL Server, and optional Azure Blob SDK calls.
  • Asynchronous messaging: no application use of a message broker or event bus was identified; a Service Bus package is declared.
  • Resilience: no explicit retry, circuit-breaker, timeout, or bulkhead policy was identified for SQL or blob operations.
  • Service discovery and gateway: no service discovery or API gateway is present; Docker Compose uses the SQL service name for local connectivity.
  • Security: OpenID Connect with Microsoft Entra ID is conditional on configuration. When that mode is disabled, a custom middleware creates a claims identity rather than authenticating credentials. No explicit TLS requirement or authorization policy for the image-upload method was identified.

Core Business Workflows

The application lets users browse a product catalog and lets catalog administrators create, update, inspect, and delete catalog items. Product images can be staged and stored separately from catalog metadata.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog ManagementProduct offered in the catalog, including price and inventory dataBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalog ManagementBrand classification used to group catalog productsCan be referenced by multiple CatalogItems
CatalogTypeCatalog ManagementProduct type classificationCan be referenced by multiple CatalogItems

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedWebFormsCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server or in-memory mock data; optional Azure Blob Storage

There are no independently deployed domain services or cross-context data exchanges in this solution. The web application is the source of truth for catalog data.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the catalog

  1. A visitor opens the catalog page, optionally providing page index and page size through the page route.
  2. The page asks ICatalogService for a paginated catalog result.
  3. The selected service implementation retrieves catalog items from EF6/SQL Server or the mock catalog list.
  4. The page resolves image URLs through IImageService, binds item data, and renders navigation links.

Workflow 2: Create or update a catalog item

  1. An administrator opens the create or edit page. When Entra ID sign-in is enabled, an unauthenticated page request initiates an OpenID Connect challenge.
  2. The administrator submits catalog and inventory values; the page checks its Web Forms model state and constructs a CatalogItem.
  3. CatalogService allocates an identifier when needed and saves the item through EF6, or the mock service mutates its in-memory list.
  4. If a staged image is supplied, the image service associates it with the item and returns the user to the catalog listing.

Workflow 3: Upload and stage an image

  1. The browser submits an image and optional item identifier to PicUploader.UploadImage.
  2. The uploader checks the decoded format against JPEG, PNG, and GIF, then asks the selected image service to stage the upload.
  3. Azure mode stores the temporary blob and returns its URL; mock mode returns the default image when no matching local catalog picture exists.
  4. During item creation or editing, the page asks the image service to move the staged image to the item location.

Workflow 4: Delete a catalog item

  1. An administrator opens the delete page for an item identifier.
  2. The page loads the item through ICatalogService and displays its details.
  3. On confirmation, the catalog service removes the entity from SQL Server or the mock list and the page redirects to the catalog.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No service-to-service aggregation or cross-service business flow was identified. The browser communicates with a single Web Forms application; that application accesses SQL Server for catalog metadata and optionally Azure Blob Storage for image content. If SQL Server is unavailable in database mode or Blob Storage is unavailable in Azure storage mode, no explicit business fallback or circuit-breaker policy is configured.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Admin as "Catalog Administrator" participant Page as "Create or Edit Page" participant Upload as "Image Uploader" participant Image as "Image Service" participant Catalog as "Catalog Service" participant DB as "Catalog Database" Admin->>Page: Enter product details opt Upload a product image Admin->>Upload: Submit image and optional item ID Upload->>Upload: Check decoded format alt Accepted raster image format Upload->>Image: Stage image Image-->>Upload: Temporary image URL Upload-->>Admin: Return image URL and name else Unsupported or invalid image Upload-->>Admin: Return HTTP 400 end end Admin->>Page: Submit catalog form Page->>Page: Check Web Forms model state Page->>Catalog: Create or update item Catalog->>DB: Persist item when database mode is active DB-->>Catalog: Save result opt Temporary image supplied Page->>Image: Associate image with catalog item end Catalog-->>Page: Operation complete Page-->>Admin: Redirect to catalog listing

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A catalog item is associated with a catalog brand and catalog type; EF mapping requires both relationships.
  • Price and stock model annotations constrain expected numeric values; page event handlers also require model-state validity before creating or saving an item.
  • The image uploader accepts decoded JPEG, PNG, or GIF formats and returns HTTP 400 for invalid image data.
  • Item identifiers are generated by the SQL HiLo sequence in database mode and incremented from the current maximum in mock mode.
  • UseMockData, UseAzureStorage, and UseAzureActiveDirectory select alternative implementations or authentication behavior.
  • Database mutations are synchronous saves through EF6. No explicit transaction orchestration across services, compensating actions, or business audit trail was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses a legacy non-SDK Web Forms project with a large packages.config dependency set. Several packages are old or use beta configuration-builder versions; the security scan also found medium-severity advisories affecting the declared log4net and IdentityModel packages. Upgrading to .NET 10 requires a Web Forms migration path rather than a framework-only target change.

Notable Observations

  • Entity Framework 6.3.0 is used with a manually configured SQL Server context; no EF Core dependency is declared.
  • Redis and Azure Service Bus packages are present, but no active cache or message-broker flow was identified in the application source/configuration.
  • Application Insights, log4net, OWIN, and Azure integrations account for multiple overlapping telemetry and platform support packages.
  • The manifest contains 147 package entries, while the project has no test-scoped package entries.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The catalog domain contains three persisted entity types backed by Entity Framework 6 and SQL Server, with an in-memory mock implementation available for local/demo configuration. Image data is stored either in the web application's local image directory or optionally in Azure Blob Storage.

Entity Model

CatalogType is mapped to the CatalogType table in Models/CatalogType.cs; CatalogBrand maps to CatalogBrand in Models/CatalogBrand.cs; and CatalogItem maps to Catalog in Models/CatalogItem.cs. CatalogDBContext configures required foreign-key relationships from catalog items to brands and types. PictureUri and TempImageName are ignored by the EF mapping.

There is no separate repository interface; CatalogService performs data access through CatalogDBContext.

Caching Strategy

No catalog query cache is configured. Mock data is held in an in-memory list by the singleton mock service. Redis and a Redis session-state provider are included as packages, but the session-state provider example in Web.config is commented out and no active Redis cache configuration was identified.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The solution contains one application domain and one catalog database; no cross-service data access or CQRS split was identified. Catalog pages call the catalog service, which queries or updates SQL Server through EF6. Image content is handled separately by the selected image service and is not stored as catalog entity content. Mock mode replaces database operations with an in-memory catalog list.
